physicssimulation.name: Physics Simulation: The Engine Behind Reality
physicssimulation.truth: Reality is continuous. Simulation is discrete. The art of physics simulation is making the discrete feel continuous — and knowing where the illusion breaks.
physicssimulation.qfep_connection: Physics simulation is the computational engine of emergence (φ). Forces (F) create order, entropy (E) dissolves it, and the simulation timestep (dt) is the hidden λ — the parameter that determines whether the system behaves or explodes. Numerical stability is the edge of chaos.
physicssimulation.demonstration: Feel Newton's laws pull you. Watch rigid bodies collide and scatter. Stretch springs until they oscillate. See force fields push particles into orbits. Pour fluid into a simulated world.
physicssimulation.description: From F=ma to fluid dynamics. Five maps covering the full stack of physics simulation: the mathematical foundations (integration methods), rigid body dynamics (collisions and constraints), elastic systems (springs and cloth), force fields (particles and n-body), and continuous matter (fluids and soft bodies). Each map adds a layer of complexity — and a new way the simulation can break.
learning_objectives: Numerical integration: Euler, Verlet, RK4 — and why the method matters
Rigid body dynamics: rotation, angular momentum, inertia tensors
Collision detection: broad phase (spatial hashing) and narrow phase (GJK/SAT)
Constraints: joints, hinges, and how physics engines solve them
Spring-mass systems: Hooke's law, damping, and emergent cloth behavior
Force fields and vector fields: invisible forces made visible
N-body simulation: gravitational democracy and the three-body problem
SPH fluid simulation: discretizing continuous matter into particles
Finite Element Method: engineering simulation for deformable bodies
Soft body physics: the compromise between rigid and fluid
content: PhysicsSim_Foundations: Newton's laws → numerical integration → Verlet. The math that makes simulation possible.
PhysicsSim_Bodies: Rigid bodies → collision detection → constraints → bouncing ball. Solid things interacting.
PhysicsSim_Springs: Mass-spring-damper → spring networks → cloth. Elastic connections and emergent softness.
PhysicsSim_Fields: Force fields → vector fields → particles → n-body → three-body problem. Invisible forces, visible chaos.
PhysicsSim_Continuum: Fluid (SPH) → FEM → soft bodies → magnetic fields → kinetic sculpture. Continuous matter, discrete approximation.
